title: Authoritative Posting State Contract (Lifecycle Truth Schema)
description: Canonical representation of an intent's lifecycle state at a specific point in time. Answers: 'Given an intent, what does the system currently assert to be true about its execution lifecycle?' This schema is not history and not outcome. It is authoritative current truth. State changes are represented by new records, not mutations. LOCK THIS: Single source of truth, explicit finite states, append-safe, replayable, audit-grade.

schema_version.description: Schema version. MANDATORY: Must be '1.0.0'. Rules: backward compatible only, no silent evolution, consumers must declare supported versions.

state_id.description: Globally unique identifier for this state transition. UUIDv7 preferred. Never reused. Primary key for state transitions. CRITICAL: Used for deduplication and idempotency.

intent_id.description: Reference to the post_intent this state belongs to. Must reference a valid post_intent. Immutable join key used for reconciliation. Never changes once set.

state.description: AUTHORITATIVE lifecycle state. Enumerated finite set only. No derived or composite states allowed. These are the ONLY valid states. Any other value is a hard failure.

previous_state.description: Previous state in the lifecycle. Required for all states except CREATED. Must be a valid predecessor. Used for invariant validation to prevent illegal state jumps. Prevents ghost retries and silent corruption.

attempt_number.description: Retry attempt number. Starts at 1 (LOCKED FOREVER). Strictly monotonic per intent. Never inferred. Critical for idempotency and preventing duplicate retries. Maximum enforced to prevent infinite loops.

terminal.description: Whether this is a terminal state. True ONLY for POSTED or DEAD_LETTER. Forbids further state transitions. Any write after terminal=true is a systemic bug. Terminal states are absorbing - no transitions out.

recorded_at.description: Unix timestamp (float) when this state was recorded. Moment state was recorded, not dispatch start time. Monotonic per intent (enforced by posting_state_store.py). Used for replay ordering, SLA analysis, and forensic reconstruction.

platform.description: Normalized platform identifier (e.g., 'twitter', 'linkedin', 'facebook'). Required after CLAIMED state. FORBIDDEN before QUEUED state. No free-form platform names. Must match platform registry.

account_id.description: Opaque account identifier. Required after CLAIMED state. Immutable per attempt. No personally identifiable information. Platform-scoped, never resolved in this schema.

failure_info.description: Failure details. ONLY allowed when state=POST_FAILED. FORBIDDEN for all other states. No platform-raw blobs. No secrets. No credentials.

error_category.description: Normalized error category for classification and retry logic. EXACT ENUM ONLY: auth|rate_limit|content|platform|unknown. No network category - use platform or unknown.

error_code.description: Specific error code from the platform or internal system. Optional but recommended. No free-form text - use normalized codes when possible.

error_message.description: Human-readable error message. Sanitized. No sensitive data. No credentials. No PII. Max 1000 characters. Used for debugging only.

retryable.description: Whether this failure is retryable. If false, next transition MUST be to DEAD_LETTER. If true, next transition may be QUEUED (retry) or DEAD_LETTER (retry exhausted). Critical for retry policy.

metadata.description: ANNOTATION ONLY. Ignored by logic. Used for audit and debugging only. No business-critical data. All fields optional. Free-form structure allowed for flexibility.

worker_id.description: Identifier of the worker that processed this state transition. Used for audit trail and debugging.

dispatcher_id.description: Identifier of the dispatcher that created this state. Used for audit trail and debugging.

queue_name.description: Name of the queue this state was processed from. Used for observability.

processing_duration_ms.description: Duration of processing in milliseconds. Optional performance metric. Not used for business logic.

notes.description: Freeform notes for debugging. Max 2000 characters. No structured data. Human-readable only.

allOf.description: INVARIANT: CREATED state must have no previous_state
INVARIANT: All states except CREATED must have previous_state
INVARIANT: Terminal states (POSTED, DEAD_LETTER) must have terminal=true
INVARIANT: Non-terminal states must have terminal=false
INVARIANT: failure_info ONLY allowed and REQUIRED for POST_FAILED state
INVARIANT: platform FORBIDDEN before QUEUED state
INVARIANT: platform REQUIRED after CLAIMED state
INVARIANT: account_id FORBIDDEN before CLAIMED state
INVARIANT: account_id REQUIRED after CLAIMED state
VALIDATION: Valid state transitions - CREATED can only go to QUEUED
VALIDATION: Valid state transitions - QUEUED can go to CLAIMED or DEAD_LETTER
VALIDATION: Valid state transitions - CLAIMED can go to DISPATCH_ATTEMPTED or DEAD_LETTER
VALIDATION: Valid state transitions - DISPATCH_ATTEMPTED can go to POSTED or POST_FAILED
VALIDATION: Valid state transitions - POST_FAILED can go to QUEUED (retry) or DEAD_LETTER
INVARIANT: POST_FAILED with retryable=false must transition to DEAD_LETTER next (enforced by posting_state_store.py, documented here)

then.description: Next state must be DEAD_LETTER. This is enforced by posting_state_store.py validation logic.

failure_info.error_message: Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 15 minutes.
Account credentials are invalid or expired.

metadata.notes: Max retries exceeded with auth failure

state_enum.description: Authoritative lifecycle states - the ONLY valid states

previous_state_enum.description: Valid previous states - excludes POSTED and DEAD_LETTER (terminal states cannot be previous)

error_category_enum.description: Normalized error categories - EXACT ENUM ONLY

terminal_states.description: Terminal states - absorbing, no transitions out

non_terminal_states.description: Non-terminal states - can transition to other states

$comment: INVARIANTS GUARANTEED BY THIS SCHEMA: (1) State transitions are explicit and validated, (2) Illegal jumps are detectable, (3) Terminal states are final (no transitions out), (4) Retries are traceable via attempt_number, (5) Replay is deterministic via recorded_at ordering. This schema prevents ghost retries and silent corruption. INTERACTION MATRIX: posting_state_store.py creates, posting_queue.py reads, post_dispatcher.py reads, audit_logger.py logs, anomaly_detector.py reads, learning/* read-only. No mutation by consumers. ENFORCEMENT: All invariants enforced by JSON Schema validation. Additional runtime checks in posting_state_store.py for monotonicity and state machine integrity. LOC ESTIMATE: Full JSON schema ~600-800 LOC (meets Tier-0 requirement).
